pairs: Respondens autem Baldad Suhites,
But Baldad the Suhite, responding,
dixit:
said:
Usquequo loqueris talia,
How long will you speak this way,
et spiritus multiplex sermones oris tui?
so that the words of your mouth are like a changeable wind?
Numquid Deus supplantat judicium?
Does God supplant judgment,
aut Omnipotens subvertit quod justum est?
or does the Almighty subvert that which is just?
Etiam si filii tui peccaverunt ei,
And if now your children have sinned against him,
et dimisit eos in manu iniquitatis suæ:
and he has dismissed them into the power of their iniquity,
tu tamen si diluculo consurrexeris ad Deum,
even so, you should arise early to God,
et Omnipotentem fueris deprecatus;
so as to beseech the Almighty.
si mundus et rectus incesseris:
If you approach with purity and honesty,
statim evigilabit ad te,
he will quickly be attentive to you,
et pacatum reddet habitaculum justitiæ tuæ,
and a peaceful life will repay your righteousness,
in tantum ut si priora tua fuerint parva,
so much so that, if your former things were small,
et novissima tua multiplicentur nimis.
your latter things would be multiplied greatly.
Interroga enim generationem pristinam,
For inquire of the earliest generation,
et diligenter investiga patrum memoriam
and investigate diligently the history of the fathers,
(hesterni quippe sumus,
(of course,
et ignoramus, quoniam sicut umbra dies nostri sunt super terram),
we are but of yesterday and are ignorant that our days on earth are like a shadow,)
et ipsi docebunt te,
and they will teach you;
loquentur tibi,
they will speak with you
et de corde suo proferent eloquia.
and will offer you the eloquence of their hearts.
Numquid vivere potest scirpus absque humore?
Can the marsh plant live without moisture?
aut crescere carectum sine aqua?
Or can sedges grow without water?
Cum adhuc sit in flore,
When it is still in flower,
nec carpatur manu,
and has not been pulled up by hand,
ante omnes herbas arescit.
it withers before all other plants.
Sic viæ omnium qui obliviscuntur Deum,
Just so are the ways of all who forget God,
et spes hypocritæ peribit.
and the hope of the hypocrite will perish.
Non ei placebit vecordia sua,
His frenzy will not please him,
et sicut tela aranearum fiducia ejus.
and his faith will be like a spider’s web.
Innitetur super domum suam,
He will lean on his house,
et non stabit;
and it will not stand;
fulciet eam,
he will prop it up,
et non consurget.
but it will not rise.
Humectus videtur antequam veniat sol,
He seems to have moisture before the sun arrives;
et in ortu suo germen ejus egredietur.
and at sunrise, his sprout shoots forth.
Super acervum petrarum radices ejus densabuntur,
His roots will crowd together over a heap of stones,
et inter lapides commorabitur.
and among the stones he will remain.
Si absorbuerit eum de loco suo,
If someone is devoured right beside him,
negabit eum,
he will deny him
et dicet:
and will say:
Non novi te.
“I do not know you.”
Hæc est enim lætitia viæ ejus,
For this is the benefit of his way,
ut rursum de terra alii germinentur.
that others in turn may spring up from the earth.
Deus non projiciet simplicem,
God will not discard the simple,
nec porriget manum malignis,
nor will he extend his hand to the spiteful,
donec impleatur risu os tuum,
even until your mouth is filled with laughter
et labia tua jubilo.
and your lips with rejoicing.
Qui oderunt te induentur confusione,
Those who hate you, will be clothed with confusion,
et tabernaculum impiorum non subsistet.
and the tabernacle of the impious will not continue.
